examples.ko: 중심을 잃은 아저씨가 어이없이 계단 아래로 굴러떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The man lost his balance and tumbled down the stairs, just like that.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 첫 경기에서 어이없이 졌어요.
examples.en: Our team lost the first game in a ridiculous way.

examples.ko: 열쇠를 어이없이 잃어버려서 하루 종일 찾았어요.
examples.en: I lost my key so stupidly that I searched for it all day.
I never thought it would end so pointlessly.
My friend canceled our plans out of nowhere, and I was surprised.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 준비한 일이 어이없이 무너져 버렸어요.
examples.en: The project I prepared for so long fell apart absurdly.

explain: '어이없다'의 부사형이고, '어이없게'로 바꿔 말해도 돼요. '어이없이'는 어떤 일이 허무하게, 황당하게 일어났다는 느낌으로 '지다, 떨어지다, 끝나다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is the adverb form of '어이없다', and you can also say '어이없게'. '어이없이' gives a feeling that something happened pointlessly or absurdly, and it goes well with verbs like '지다' (lose), '떨어지다' (fall) and '끝나다' (end).

examples.ko: 너무 오래 앉아 있다가 일어났더니 머리가 어질어질해요.
examples.en: I stood up after sitting too long, and my head is spinning.

examples.ko: 어제 잠을 못 자서 아침부터 어질어질했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep last night, so I felt dizzy from the morning.
If you feel dizzy, sit down and rest for a moment.

examples.ko: 배를 타면 속이 울렁거리고 어질어질할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: On a boat, my stomach churns and I sometimes feel dizzy.

examples.ko: 빈속에 커피를 마셨더니 눈앞이 어질어질해서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I drank coffee on an empty stomach, and I was startled when everything went dizzy.

examples.ko: 사람이 너무 많은 곳에 있으면 어질어질해져요.
examples.en: I get dizzy when I'm in a place with too many people.

explain: '어지럽다'보다 머리가 빙글빙글 도는 느낌을 생생하게 말할 때 써요. '어질어질해지다'처럼 갑자기 그런 상태가 되는 것도 말할 수 있어요. 몸이 안 좋을 때뿐 아니라 놀이기구나 높은 곳에서도 써요.
explain_en: Use it instead of '어지럽다' (dizzy) when you want to describe the head-spinning feeling vividly. '어질어질해지다' says that you suddenly become dizzy. You can use it not only when you are unwell but also on rides or in high places.

examples.ko: 친구가 어쩌고저쩌고 계속 말하는데 하나도 못 들었어요.
examples.en: My friend kept going blah-blah-blah, and I didn't hear any of it.
Mom nagged me for a while, saying blah-blah-blah about studying.
He just rattled off excuses, yadda-yadda-yadda.

examples.ko: 회의에서 어쩌고저쩌고 얘기가 길었지만 결론은 없었어요.
examples.en: The meeting had a long blah-blah-blah, but there was no conclusion.

examples.ko: 어쩌고저쩌고 말만 많고 행동은 안 해요.
examples.en: He talks a lot, blah-blah-blah, but doesn't act.

examples.ko: 그 애가 나한테 어쩌고저쩌고 하더니 그냥 가 버렸어요.
examples.en: She said something blah-blah-blah to me and just left.

explain: 남이 한 긴 말을 다 옮기기 귀찮을 때 줄여서 흉내 내는 말이에요. '이러쿵저러쿵'과 비슷하지만, 이 말은 들은 말을 대신하는 느낌이 강해요. 격식 있는 글보다 편한 대화에서 써요.
explain_en: People use it to skip over a long speech they don't want to repeat in full. It is similar to '이러쿵저러쿵', but this one feels more like standing in for the words you heard. It fits casual conversation better than formal writing.

examples.en: Don't grumble behind my back; tell me directly.
He started complaining again, going on and on.
Whenever I meet him, he starts yammering on.

examples.ko: 아까부터 옆자리 사람들이 어쩌고저쩌고하는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I've been hearing the people next to me yammering since a while ago.
Going on about it is useless, so please stop.

examples.ko: 동생이 어쩌고저쩌고했지만 저는 듣는 척만 했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling went on and on, but I only pretended to listen.

explain: 불만이나 별 쓸모없는 말을 길게 늘어놓는 모습에 써요. 말하는 사람을 조금 못마땅하게 보는 느낌이 있어서, 윗사람에게 쓰면 무례할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes someone going on and on with complaints or useless talk. It carries a slightly disapproving tone toward the speaker, so it can be rude if used about a superior.

en: be suppressed; be controlled; be contained

examples.ko: 오랫동안 억눌려 있던 감정이 한꺼번에 터져 나왔어요.
examples.en: Feelings that had been suppressed for a long time burst out all at once.

examples.ko: 엄격한 집안 분위기 때문에 아이들의 의견이 억눌려요.
examples.en: The strict atmosphere at home suppresses the children's opinions.
My anger was bottled up, and my chest felt tight.

examples.ko: 억눌린 사람들의 목소리를 들어 줘야 해요.
examples.en: We should listen to the voices of people who are oppressed.

examples.ko: 시험 걱정에 억눌리면 평소 실력도 나오지 않아요.
examples.en: If you're weighed down by exam worries, you can't show your usual ability.

examples.ko: 억눌렸던 꿈을 다시 꺼내 보기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to bring out the dream I had kept down.

explain: '억누르다'(감정을 억누르다)에 대응하는 말로, 감정·욕구·목소리 같은 것이 주어가 돼요. 사람이 일부러 누를 때는 '억누르다'를 써요. '억눌린 감정'처럼 '억눌린 ~' 형태로도 써요.
explain_en: It pairs with '억누르다' (to hold down, as in holding down feelings); here the thing being held down, such as an emotion, desire or voice, is the subject. When a person deliberately presses something down, use '억누르다'. It also appears as '억눌린 ~', as in '억눌린 감정'.

examples.en: The way home is a steep hill road.

examples.ko: 아이들이 송아지를 끌고 꼬부라진 언덕길을 올라오고 있어요.
examples.en: The children are coming up the winding hill road, leading a calf.

examples.ko: 언덕길에서 자전거를 타면 내려갈 때 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: When you ride a bike on a hill road, you have to be careful going down.

examples.ko: 눈이 오면 언덕길이 미끄러워서 차가 못 다녀요.
examples.en: When it snows, the hill road is slippery and cars can't get through.
Every evening I take a slow walk along the hill road in my neighborhood.

examples.ko: 언덕길 끝에 작은 카페가 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small cafe at the end of the hill road.

explain: '오르막길', '내리막길'은 가는 방향에 초점이 있고, '언덕길'은 언덕에 나 있는 길 자체를 말해서 오르내리는 길 모두를 가리켜요. 그래서 올라갈 때도 내려갈 때도 '언덕길'이라고 할 수 있어요.
explain_en: '오르막길' (uphill road) and '내리막길' (downhill road) focus on the direction you travel, while '언덕길' refers to the road on a hill itself, so it covers both going up and coming down.

examples.en: My uncle worked in the media world for twenty years.
People in the press are sensitive to new information.

examples.ko: 그 일 때문에 언론계가 한동안 시끄러웠어요.
examples.en: Because of that matter, the press world was noisy for a while.
I wanted to go into the media, so I applied to a newspaper company.

examples.ko: 언론계에 오래 계신 선배가 조언해 줬어요.
examples.en: A senior who has been in the press for a long time gave me advice.
Changes in the media world are fast, so it's hard to keep up.

explain: 신문·방송·잡지에서 일하는 사람들과 그 세계를 한꺼번에 가리켜요. '-계'는 '연예계', '정치계'처럼 어떤 분야의 사람들이 모인 세계를 말할 때 붙어요. '언론'은 보도하는 활동이나 기관 자체를 말해서 쓰임이 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to the people and the world of newspapers, broadcasting and magazines as a whole. The suffix '-계' is attached to a field to mean its world, as in '연예계' (entertainment world) and '정치계' (political world). '언론' by itself means the press activity or institutions, so it is used a little differently.

examples.en: He is a famous linguist who studies Korean.

examples.ko: 언어학자가 되려면 대학에서 언어학을 공부해야 해요.
examples.en: To become a linguist, you have to study linguistics at university.
The class taught by the professor, who is a linguist, is the most fun.
Linguists observe how language changes.
I've dreamed of becoming a linguist since I was little.

examples.ko: 언어학자의 설명을 들으니 문법이 쉽게 이해됐어요.
examples.en: After hearing the linguist's explanation, I understood the grammar easily.

explain: 외국어를 잘하는 사람이나 통역사와는 달라요. 언어 자체의 구조나 변화를 연구하는 사람을 말해요. 그래서 여러 언어를 못해도 언어학자가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: This is different from someone who is good at foreign languages or an interpreter. A linguist studies the structure and change of language itself, so a person can be a linguist without speaking many languages.

examples.en: There is a grain of rice around your mouth.

examples.ko: 해 질 무렵 마을 언저리까지 걸어갔어요.
examples.en: At sunset, I walked to the edge of the village.

examples.ko: 기억 언저리에서 맴돌 뿐 이름이 생각 안 나요.
examples.en: It's just circling at the edge of my memory, and I can't recall the name.

examples.ko: 눈 언저리가 빨개진 걸 보니 울었나 봐요.
examples.en: The area around your eyes is red, so you must have been crying.

examples.ko: 우리가 아는 건 진실의 언저리일 뿐이에요.
examples.en: What we know is only the fringe of the truth.
Many people get married around thirty.

explain: '가장자리'가 물건의 끝을 말한다면, '언저리'는 그 끝 주변까지 넓게 가리켜요. 입 언저리, 눈 언저리처럼 몸에도 쓰고, '서른 언저리'처럼 나이나 시기를 어림잡을 때도 써요.
explain_en: While '가장자리' points to the very edge of an object, '언저리' covers the area around that edge. It is used for the body, as in 입 언저리 (around the mouth), and also to estimate an age or time, as in '서른 언저리' (around thirty).

en: live at someone's place as a dependent; live off others

examples.ko: 남의 집에 몇 년 얹혀살았더니 눈치만 늘었어요.
examples.en: After living at someone else's house for a few years, all that grew was my sense of reading the room.

examples.ko: 돈을 모을 때까지 친구 집에 얹혀살고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm staying at a friend's place until I save up some money.
I feel sorry now about living off my parents.
How long are you going to live at your brother's place?

examples.ko: 대학 때 이모 댁에 얹혀산 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once stayed with my aunt's family during college.

examples.ko: 얹혀살면 집세는 안 내도 마음이 편하진 않아요.
examples.en: When you live in someone's home, you don't pay rent, but it's not comfortable.

explain: 집세를 내지 않고 남의 집에서 신세를 지며 산다는 느낌이라서 미안함이나 눈치를 보는 마음이 같이 따라와요. '부모님께 얹혀살다'처럼 '~에/께 얹혀살다' 형태로 자주 써요. 비슷한 표현으로 '신세를 지다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of living in someone else's home without paying your own way, so guilt and watching others' moods often come with it. It usually takes the form '~에/께 얹혀살다', like '부모님께 얹혀살다'. A similar expression is '신세를 지다' (to be indebted to someone).

examples.en: Maybe I washed it wrong, because the white shirt is blotchy.
I have a cat with a mottled pattern.
The paint was applied unevenly on the wall.
My face got blotchy from sunburn.
It rained, so the road was spotted with wet patches.
Please apply it evenly so it doesn't look blotchy.

explain: 색이 고르지 않고 얼룩이 진 모습이에요. '알록달록'은 여러 고운 색이 섞인 예쁜 모습이라서, 색이 고르지 않아 지저분해 보일 때는 '얼룩덜룩'을 써요.
explain_en: It describes color that is uneven and patchy. '알록달록' means many pretty colors mixed together, so use '얼룩덜룩' when the color is uneven and looks messy.

examples.en: Coffee splashed on my white clothes and stained them.

examples.ko: 눈물로 얼룩진 얼굴을 보고 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: It hurt to see her tear-stained face.
The wall is stained because of moisture.
Eat carefully so you don't stain it.

examples.ko: 이 천은 물에 닿으면 쉽게 얼룩져요.
examples.en: This fabric stains easily when it touches water.

examples.ko: 싸움으로 얼룩졌던 지난 한 해를 잊고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to forget last year, which was marred by fights.

explain: '더러워지다'보다 자국이 남는다는 느낌이 강해요. '눈물로 얼룩지다', '슬픔으로 얼룩진 하루'처럼 좋지 않은 일이 가득 찬 시간을 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It carries a stronger sense than '더러워지다' (get dirty) that a mark is left behind. It is also used figuratively for a time filled with bad things, as in '눈물로 얼룩지다' (be stained with tears) and '슬픔으로 얼룩진 하루' (a day marred by sadness).

examples.ko: 너무 놀라서 얼빠진 표정으로 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I was so shocked that I just stood there with a dazed look.

examples.ko: 왜 그렇게 얼빠져 있어요? 무슨 일 있어요?
examples.en: Why are you so spaced out? Is something wrong?

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나자 얼빠졌는지 계속 멍하니 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: After the exam ended, I kept sitting blankly, as if my mind had left me.
Don't zone out; snap out of it.
I was dumbstruck when I saw the celebrity and stared for a long time.
It was a landscape so beautiful it left me spellbound.

explain: 놀람, 충격, 넋을 빼앗길 만큼 푹 빠진 상태에서 멍해진 모습을 말해요. '얼이 빠지다'라고도 해요. 남에게 쓰면 조금 흉보는 말투가 될 수 있으니 윗사람에게 직접 쓰지 마세요.
explain_en: It describes being blank and spaced out from surprise, shock or being utterly absorbed in something. You can also say '얼이 빠지다'. Said about another person it can sound a bit like teasing, so do not use it directly toward a superior.

examples.en: My eardrums tingled for a moment from the shout.
I ate spicy tteokbokki, and my tongue is burning and numb.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 귀가 얼얼해요.
examples.en: I was outside on a cold day, and my ears are stinging.

examples.ko: 세게 부딪혀서 이마가 얼얼해서 한참 문질렀어요.
examples.en: I bumped my forehead hard, and it stung, so I rubbed it for a while.
The malatang is so numbingly hot, but it's delicious.

examples.ko: 얼얼하던 손이 따뜻한 물에 담그니 풀렸어요.
examples.en: My numb, stinging hand loosened up when I soaked it in warm water.

explain: 매운 음식, 추위, 부딪친 아픔 때문에 그 부분이 따끔하고 감각이 무뎌진 느낌이에요. 맛에는 '얼얼한 맛'처럼 매워서 혀가 마비되는 듯한 느낌을 말하고, 그냥 '맵다'보다 감각이 둔해지는 느낌이 더해져요.
explain_en: It describes a part of the body feeling stinging and dulled from spicy food, cold or a knock. For taste, '얼얼한 맛' means a spiciness that makes the tongue feel numb, adding a dulled sensation to plain '맵다' (spicy).

examples.en: I fell on the ice and hurt my knee.
In winter the river freezes and becomes a sheet of ice.
The children ride sleds on the ice.
I crossed the ice, walking very carefully.
The road was completely icy, so it was scary to drive.
I went to the ice to skate.

explain: 얼어붙은 강, 호수, 길 위를 가리켜요. '빙판'과 거의 같게 쓰고, 길이 얼었을 때는 '빙판길'이라고도 말해요. '얼음판 같다'처럼 길이 몹시 미끄러울 때 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the frozen surface of a river, lake or road. It is used almost the same as '빙판', and an icy road is also called '빙판길'. You can also say '얼음판 같다' figuratively when a road is extremely slippery.

examples.ko: 관아로 찾아가는 사람들이 얼추 백 명이나 됐어요.
examples.en: The people heading to the government office numbered about a hundred.

examples.ko: 공연장에 사람이 얼추 천 명은 왔어요.
examples.en: Roughly a thousand people came to the concert hall.
My homework is almost done.

examples.ko: 얼추 계산해 봐도 십만 원은 넘어요.
examples.en: Even by a rough calculation, it's over a hundred thousand won.

examples.ko: 여기서 역까지 얼추 십 분쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes roughly ten minutes from here to the station.

examples.ko: 그 사람 나이가 저랑 얼추 비슷해요.
examples.en: He is about the same age as me.

explain: 정확하지는 않지만 거의 맞는 수나 정도를 말할 때 써요. '대략'과 비슷한데 더 편한 대화 느낌이 있어요. 숫자 앞에서는 '얼추 백 명', '비슷하다·끝나다' 같은 말 앞에서는 '거의 다'라는 뜻이 돼요.
explain_en: It means a number or degree that isn't exact but is nearly right. It is like '대략' but has a more casual, conversational feel. Before a number it means 'about', and before words like '비슷하다' (similar) or '끝나다' (end) it means 'almost'.

examples.ko: 이어폰 줄이 얽히고설켜서 풀 수가 없어요.
examples.en: The earphone cord is so tangled that I can't undo it.
The stories of the two families are intertwined.
If things get tangled, sort them out one by one.
It was hard to sort out the tangled relationships.
This drama is about characters whose lives get entangled.
The problem that had been so tangled has finally been resolved.

explain: 실이나 줄이 엉키는 모습뿐 아니라 관계, 사건, 이해관계가 복잡하게 이어진 것에도 써요. 단순히 '엉키다'보다 매우 복잡하다는 느낌이 강해서 풀기 힘든 상황에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes not only threads or cords getting tangled but also relationships, events and interests that are connected in a complicated way. It sounds stronger than a simple '엉키다' (get tangled), so it suits situations that are hard to unravel.

en: exaggerate pain; feign pain; make great fuss about nothing

examples.en: Are you already making a fuss before you've even had the shot?

examples.ko: 조금 긁힌 걸로 너무 엄살떨지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't make such a fuss over a little scratch.
My younger sibling makes a big deal even about a cold.
Even if you exaggerate like that, nobody will help you.

examples.ko: 어제는 엄살떤 게 아니라 정말 아팠어요.
examples.en: Yesterday I wasn't exaggerating; it really hurt.
He complains of pain to get out of working.

explain: 보통 '엄살을 떨다', '엄살을 부리다'처럼 목적어를 넣어서도 말해요. 아프지 않은데 아픈 척하거나 작은 일을 크게 말하는 것인데, 상대에게 쓰면 기분이 상할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is also commonly said with an object, as in '엄살을 떨다' or '엄살을 부리다'. It is about acting hurt when you're not, or making a small thing sound big, and it can offend the other person if used toward them.

examples.en: I slipped on the ice and landed on my bottom.

examples.ko: 엉덩방아 때문에 하루 종일 엉덩이가 아팠어요.
examples.en: My bottom hurt all day because of the fall.

examples.ko: 스케이트를 처음 탔을 때 엉덩방아만 여러 번 찧었어요.
examples.en: The first time I skated, I did nothing but fall on my bottom many times.

examples.ko: 엉덩방아를 찧은 모습이 웃겨서 다 같이 웃었어요.
examples.en: The way he fell on his bottom was funny, so we all laughed.
I walked slowly in case I'd end up sitting down hard.
I fell on my bottom, but luckily I wasn't hurt.

explain: 거의 '엉덩방아를 찧다'라는 말로만 써요. 뒤로 주저앉으면서 엉덩이부터 땅에 떨어지는 모습이고, 조금 우스꽝스러운 느낌이 있어서 가볍게 웃으며 말할 때 많이 어울려요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in the phrase '엉덩방아를 찧다'. It pictures falling backward and landing on your bottom first, and it has a slightly comical feel, so it suits a light, humorous tone.

examples.ko: 컵을 엎지르면 바로 닦아야 얼룩이 안 생겨요.
examples.en: If you spill a cup, wipe it up right away so it doesn't stain.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 커피를 엎지르고 놀라서 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: I spilled coffee on the desk and cried out in surprise.

examples.ko: 엎지르지 않게 컵을 두 손으로 잡으세요.
examples.en: Hold the cup with both hands so you don't spill it.
I spilled the soup, so I had to change my clothes.

examples.ko: 엎지른 물을 닦다 보니 시간이 다 갔어요.
examples.en: Wiping up the spilled water took all my time.
You could spill it if you're careless, so be careful.

explain: '르' 불규칙이라서 '엎질러요, 엎질렀어요'로 활용해요. '쏟다'는 일부러 부을 때도 쓰지만 '엎지르다'는 보통 실수로 그릇이 기울어 흘릴 때 써요. 사람이 주어이고, 물건이 저절로 쏟아지면 '엎질러지다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a '르' irregular verb, so it conjugates as '엎질러요' and '엎질렀어요'. '쏟다' can be used for pouring on purpose, but '엎지르다' is normally for tipping a container by mistake. A person is the subject; when something spills by itself, use '엎질러지다'.

examples.en: The water bottle spilled inside the bag.

examples.ko: 컵이 쓰러지면서 우유가 엎질러져서 바닥이 젖었어요.
examples.en: The cup fell over and the milk spilled, so the floor got wet.

examples.ko: 엎질러진 우유를 닦는 동안 아이는 울지 않았어요.
examples.en: The child didn't cry while I wiped up the spilled milk.
It'd be a mess if the soup bowl spilled, so I walk slowly.

examples.ko: 물이 엎질러지는 소리에 놀라 부엌으로 달려갔어요.
examples.en: Startled by the sound of water spilling, I ran to the kitchen.

examples.ko: 그릇이 엎질러질 것 같아서 얼른 잡았어요.
examples.en: The bowl looked like it would spill, so I quickly grabbed it.

explain: '엎지르다'는 사람이 주어이고, '엎질러지다'는 물이나 그릇 같은 것이 주어로 나와요. 그래서 실수한 사람을 말하지 않고 일어난 일만 말하고 싶을 때 써요. '엎질러진 물'은 되돌릴 수 없는 일을 비유하는 말로도 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 벌어져서 되돌릴 수 없는 일을 말할 때 써요. 후회하는 사람에게 위로하거나 이제 그만 생각하라고 할 때 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that has already happened and can't be undone. It comes up when comforting someone who regrets it or telling them to let it go.
phrases.en_equiv: It's no use crying over spilled milk.

explain_en: With '엎지르다' a person is the subject, while with '엎질러지다' the water or container is. Use it when you want to describe what happened without naming who made the mistake. '엎질러진 물' is also used figuratively for something that can't be undone.

examples.en: I had an X-ray exam at the hospital.

examples.ko: 엑스선으로 찍으면 뼈 상태를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: With an X-ray, you can see the condition of the bones.

examples.ko: 엑스선은 눈에 보이지 않지만 몸을 통과해요.
examples.en: X-rays are invisible, but they pass through the body.
At the airport, you put your bag through an X-ray machine.

examples.ko: 엑스선 사진을 보니 다행히 부러지지 않았대요.
examples.en: The X-ray picture shows that, luckily, it isn't broken.
At the dentist, they took an X-ray and checked for cavities.

explain: 병원에서는 '엑스레이'라는 말을 더 많이 써요. 사진은 '엑스레이 사진', 찍는 것은 '엑스레이를 찍다'라고 해요. '엑스선'은 그 빛(전자기파)의 이름이라 설명문이나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: At hospitals people more often say '엑스레이'. The image is called '엑스레이 사진' and taking one is '엑스레이를 찍다'. '엑스선' is the name of the ray itself, so it appears more in explanations and the news.

examples.ko: 운동을 하면 엔도르핀이 나와서 기분이 좋아져요.
examples.en: When you exercise, endorphins are released and you feel better.
They say laughter makes your body release endorphins.

examples.ko: 맛있는 걸 먹으면 엔도르핀 덕분에 기분이 좋아지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: When I eat something tasty, it feels like the endorphins lift my mood.

examples.ko: 엔도르핀이 부족할 땐 좋아하는 노래를 들어요.
examples.en: When I'm low on endorphins, I listen to my favorite songs.

examples.ko: 엔도르핀처럼 기분을 올려 주는 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: I have a friend who lifts my mood like a shot of endorphins.

examples.ko: 엔도르핀은 몸이 아플 때도 아픔을 줄여 줘요.
examples.en: Endorphins also ease pain when the body hurts.

explain: 과학 용어지만 일상에서도 '엔도르핀이 돈다'처럼 기분이 좋아지고 활기가 생기는 느낌을 가볍게 말할 때 써요. 운동, 웃음, 맛있는 음식 이야기에서 잘 나와요.
explain_en: It is a scientific term, but in daily life people use it lightly, as in '엔도르핀이 돈다', to mean that mood and energy are rising. It comes up often when talking about exercise, laughter and tasty food.

examples.en: This weekend our club is going on an overnight trip.
At the trip, we played games and talked all night.
We chose a pension in Gangwon-do for the trip.

examples.ko: 신입생 엠티에 가면 친구를 빨리 사귈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go on the freshman trip, you can make friends quickly.

examples.ko: 엠티 때 입을 편한 옷을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I packed comfortable clothes to wear on the trip.

examples.ko: 엠티가 끝나고 집에 오니 너무 피곤했어요.
examples.en: When I got home after the trip, I was exhausted.

explain: 대학교 동아리, 학과, 회사 사람들이 함께 1박 이상 놀러 가는 모임을 말해요. 보통 '엠티를 가다'라고 해요. 한국에서 만든 줄임말이라 영어권에서는 이 뜻으로 잘 통하지 않아요.
explain_en: It means a gathering where members of a university club, department or company travel together for at least one night. People usually say '엠티를 가다'. It is an abbreviation made in Korea, so it is not understood in this sense in English-speaking countries.

examples.ko: 대문을 여닫는 소리가 들리는 걸 보니 아들이 외출하나 봐요.
examples.en: I hear the gate opening and closing, so my son must be going out.

examples.ko: 서랍을 자꾸 여닫지 말고 필요한 것만 꺼내세요.
examples.en: Don't keep opening and closing the drawer; just take out what you need.

examples.ko: 문을 세게 여닫으면 이웃에게 방해가 돼요.
examples.en: If you open and close the door hard, it disturbs the neighbors.

examples.ko: 문을 하루에도 몇 번씩 여닫아도 고장 안 나요.
examples.en: Even if you open and close the door several times a day, it won't break.

examples.ko: 창문을 여닫을 때 손이 끼지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to get your hand caught when you open and close the window.
I want to buy a bag that's easy to open and close.

explain: 문, 서랍, 창문, 뚜껑처럼 열고 닫는 것에 써요. 한 번 열기만 할 때는 '열다', 닫기만 할 때는 '닫다'를 써요. 열고 닫는 동작이 반복되거나 함께 이어질 때 '여닫다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Use it for things that open and shut, such as doors, drawers, windows and lids. When you only open, use '열다', and when you only close, use '닫다'. '여닫다' is natural when the opening and closing happens repeatedly or together.

examples.en: The queen bee lays eggs.
The worker bees gather food for the queen bee.

examples.ko: 벌집 한가운데에서 여왕벌과 일벌들이 함께 살아요.
examples.en: In the middle of the hive, the queen bee and worker bees live together.
They say the hive falls into disorder when the queen bee disappears.

examples.ko: 저는 여왕벌보다 일벌이 더 대단하다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think worker bees are more impressive than the queen bee.
In science class, we learned about the life of the queen bee.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '일벌'과 '수벌'이에요. 한 벌집에는 보통 여왕벌이 한 마리 있어요. 과학 시간이나 자연 이야기에서 주로 나와요.
explain_en: Its related words are '일벌' (worker bee) and '수벌' (drone). A hive normally has one queen bee. It appears mainly in science class and nature talk.

examples.en: On a clear day, I suddenly got caught in a sun shower.

examples.ko: 여우비는 금방 그치니까 우산 없이 기다려 봐요.
examples.en: A sun shower stops soon, so let's wait without an umbrella.
After the sun shower, a rainbow appeared in the sky.
The sun was bright and yet a sun shower fell, which was amazing.

examples.ko: 여우비 때문에 잠깐 처마 밑에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: Because of the sun shower, I stood under the eaves for a moment.
It was just a sun shower today, so I ran without an umbrella.

explain: 해가 떠 있는데 잠깐 내리다 그치는 비예요. 오래 쏟아지는 '소나기'와 달리 날이 맑은 채로 금방 지나가는 비를 말해요. 날씨 이야기에서 가볍게 쓰는 순우리말이에요.
explain_en: It is rain that falls briefly while the sun is out. Unlike a '소나기' (shower) that pours hard, this is rain that passes quickly while the sky stays clear. It is a native Korean word used lightly in weather talk.

examples.en: If there's something you don't know, ask your teacher.
I'd like to ask Grandmother how her health is.

examples.ko: 길을 모를 때는 어른께 여쭈어보면 친절하게 알려 주실 거예요.
examples.en: When you don't know the way, if you ask an adult, they'll kindly tell you.
I'll ask the department head first.
Asking the professor questions still makes me nervous.
I'm calling to ask about the schedule.

explain: '물어보다'의 높임말로, 선생님·어른·직장 상사처럼 윗사람에게 물을 때 써요. 말할 때는 '여쭤보다'로 줄여서 많이 말해요. 나를 낮추는 말이라 친구나 아랫사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is the honorific form of '물어보다', used when asking a teacher, an elder or a boss. In speech it is often shortened to '여쭤보다'. Because it humbles the speaker, don't use it toward friends or people younger than you.

examples.en: I enjoy listening to my grandfather's travel stories.
My friend's stories about traveling in Europe were really fun.
Long travel stories make me sleepy as I listen.
I'm filling my blog with travel stories.
The photos are nice, but please also tell me your travel stories.
In travel stories, even mistakes become something to laugh about.

explain: 여행을 다녀온 사람이 들려주는 이야기를 말해요. 글로 쓴 기록인 '여행기'와 달리 말로 이야기하는 느낌이 강해서, '여행담을 늘어놓다', '여행담을 듣다'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It means the stories a person tells after coming back from a trip. Unlike '여행기', which is a written record, it feels more like telling the stories out loud, so it is often used in '여행담을 늘어놓다' (go on telling travel stories) and '여행담을 듣다'.

examples.en: I lifted a barbell at the gym.
With a barbell, start with a light one at first.
My younger sibling is a weightlifter who lifts barbells.

examples.ko: 역기로 운동한 지 석 달이 됐어요.
examples.en: It's been three months since I started working out with a barbell.

examples.ko: 올림픽에서 역기를 번쩍 드는 선수를 보고 감동했어요.
examples.en: I was moved watching an athlete lift a barbell overhead at the Olympics.
It's fine to work out with dumbbells instead of a barbell.

explain: 헬스장에서는 '바벨'이라고도 많이 말해요. 운동 종목 이름은 '역도'이고, '역기'는 그때 쓰는 기구예요. 그래서 '역기를 들다'라고 하고, '역도를 들다'라고는 하지 않아요.
explain_en: At the gym people also commonly say '바벨'. The sport is called '역도', and '역기' is the equipment used in it. So you say '역기를 들다', not '역도를 들다'.

examples.en: The signs of exhaustion were plain on his face.
The nervousness is clear on your face.
You obviously look tired, so please rest a bit.

examples.ko: 실망한 흔적이 역력해서 말을 걸기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The disappointment was so obvious that it was hard to speak to him.
It was plain to see that she had been crying.
He clearly didn't like it, but he helped until the end.

explain: 피로, 긴장, 실망 같은 마음이나 흔적이 겉으로 뚜렷이 드러날 때 써요. 주어는 보통 '기색, 흔적, 티, 표정'처럼 눈으로 보이는 것이에요. 사물이 선명할 때 쓰는 '선명하다'와는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: Use it when a feeling or sign such as fatigue, tension or disappointment shows plainly on the outside. The subject is usually something visible, like '기색', '흔적', '티' or '표정'. It differs from '선명하다', which is for objects that look sharp or vivid.

examples.en: Our team suffered a come-from-behind loss in the second half.

examples.ko: 이길 줄 알았는데 역전패라니 믿기지 않아요.
examples.en: I thought we'd win, so I can't believe it's a comeback loss.

examples.ko: 역전패 때문에 응원하던 사람들이 모두 말이 없었어요.
examples.en: Because of the reversal loss, all the fans were silent.
We were ahead 3-0 and then lost in a reversal.
The regret of the comeback loss stayed with me for a long time.
That game ended in a reversal loss, and I was upset.

explain: 반대말은 '역전승'이에요. 처음에 앞서고 있다가 뒤집혀서 질 때만 쓰기 때문에, 처음부터 계속 진 경기에는 쓰지 않아요. '역전패를 당하다' 또는 '역전패하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '역전승' (a comeback win). It is used only when a side was ahead at first and then lost after the game turned around, so it isn't used for a game that was lost from the start. You say '역전패를 당하다' or '역전패하다'.
